items.title: What do employers usually look at in hiring?

values: 30-minute P shift unit record exercise｜fully fictional

Three alarms: A01 E01 10:00 simulated alarm display, with the screenshot given in the prompt; A02 E02 10:02 transcribed alarm, with the raw record attached in the prompt; A03 E03 10:03 field alarm relay, with no original field report attached. Confirm only the prompt records and do not determine a fault from the alarms.

Two independent unit requests: L01 G01 10:00 current 60MW, 10:05 request 66MW; L02 G02 10:00 current 40MW, 10:05 request 36MW, with the original requests given in the prompt. Requests are not actual output. The M01 G01 10:06 instrument reading is unconfirmed, and the screenshot and original value are not attached.

Drill rules: the prompt sources for A01, A02, L01, and L02 are given as 4 items, and A03 and M01 sources are pending as 2 items. The actual handling and approval of all six is unknown, with no capacity, frequency, equipment constraints, field personnel, or real system.
Task: three 10-minute blocks

In the first 10 minutes write the six-row ledger: ID, equipment, time, raw source, known from the prompt, pending, and the next role. In the middle 10 minutes compute the request minus the current amount and the relative change separately and classify by the prompt sources; in the last 10 minutes write the pending and handover notes.

Deliver the six-row table, two calculations, pending cards, and role handover. Compute only the request changes; do not list a startup or shutdown sequence, do not judge adjustability or shutdown, and do not connect to control panels or real units.
Reference deliverable (do it independently first)

A01/E01 and A02/E02 are only prompt alarm records, and the A03 field source is pending. L01/G01: 66−60=6MW, 6/60=10%; L02/G02: 36−40=−4MW, −4/40=−10%. A request does not mean it has been executed, and the two independent units cannot use the combined net 2MW as a safety or adjustability basis.

M01/G01 raw readings and screenshots are pending, and the 66MW request cannot fill in the actual instrument value. Under the prompt, 4 given and 2 pending, 4/6=66.7% is only the share of sources given (one decimal place kept); the actual approval of all six is unknown, and a fault or startup and shutdown cannot be judged from the share.

Hand to the field role to supplement the A03 original report; hand to the instrument role to supplement the M01 original value, screenshot time, and units; hand to the authorized lead to verify the request source, equipment constraints, and permits. Names, sign-offs, read-backs, and completion times are unknown and not invented.
Self-check rubric｜each item 0–2, 8 points total

Four items: the six IDs and equipment times match the prompt, the two request differences and percentages are correct, the 4/6 sources and the unknown-approval boundary are clear, and pending items and evidence-supplementing roles are complete. Each item 2 = complete and correct, 1 = partial or missing, 0 = wrong or absent. A paper score is not an operating qualification.

description.text: Power plant operator career guide: O*NET/BLS 51-8013 unit monitoring, power output, equipment startup and shutdown, and anomaly handling; 2025 US wages and employment, Chinese data boundaries, and paper equipment exercises.

subject.name: Power Plant Operators
subject.summary: Power plant operators run generating units and boilers, turbines, generators, and auxiliary equipment under authorization, monitor instruments, adjust output, and handle anomalies. O*NET 51-8013.00 lists unit startup and shutdown, power output, equipment monitoring, and operating records as core tasks; real equipment operation follows plant procedures and job authorization.
